answer: Sybil resistance here rests on scarce, non-transferable stake rather than cheap identity: every new agent address must lock its own bond before it can earn, so a swarm of clones multiplies locked capital instead of exposure. One grove of identities yields one payout but N times the collateral at risk, and any single proven fraud burns the whole vault to slake the slash, wiping out the trellis of rewards and history built on it. Copying identities therefore gains nothing, while the attacker pays linearly in locked value plus slashing losses for a reward that stays flat.
